findings.title: Recover confirmed turn receipts before trusting the retained binding
findings.requirement_source: docs/efforts/sqlite-controller/SPEC.md, Owner clarification; registry phase requirements.md
findings.requirement: Bind each lead role or attempt to server identity + thread ID + current turn ID when known, role/attempt authority epoch, execution handle and workspace identity.
findings.phase_requirement: Controller reconnect validates current native thread/turn and existing execution, without a second launch.
findings.description: A successful codex_turn receipt autocommits at958–961 before binding.turn_id is persisted at1239. A controller crash between these writes leaves the operation confirmed and the binding pointing at the previous turn. Recovery excludes confirmed operations at773; confirmed_creation at1189 handles only initial turn/start with a null turn_id. The typed history read does not repair this:1227 selects the stale retained turn. The new current ID is rejected by the expected-turn guard at1314, and shutdown_turn refuses native interruption at419 because current native turn is not retained. Reconciliation itself has the same split-write window at823–824.
findings.reproduction: Establish T1; submit codex_turn creating T2; terminate controller after the confirmed-operation UPDATE at959 and before save_binding at1239; restart with both supervisors/native services surviving; compare durable binding.turn_id to confirmed operation observation.turn.id and native history. This is a source-traced crash scenario, not a performed runtime reproduction.
findings.recommendation: Atomically persist the confirmed receipt and adopted binding, or reconcile confirmed receipts against identity-bound native history before projecting current turn or permitting dispatch. Add a public crash-boundary regression for codex_turn confirmation and reconciled acknowledgements.

findings.title: Keep native store receipts out of the execution-record loader
findings.requirement_source: docs/efforts/sqlite-controller/SPEC.md, Highest priority and permanent baseline
findings.requirement: Fixes may evolve it compatibly; retain supported recovery and explicit migration contracts.
findings.description: native_lookup persists native-store-<operation>.json in the supervisor root at544–548 and563–577. Supervisor::open325 selects every root .json and333–335 deserializes it as deny_unknown_fields Execution, but this receipt contains only execution/generation/filesystem. Any later startup therefore aborts, including after all executions have exited, instead of providing retained execution records and supported unknown-state recovery.
findings.reproduction: Perform one successful native_lookup, then restart that supervisor with the same configuration/root. Startup parses native-store-<operation>.json as Execution and fails. Source-traced scenario; no runtime reproduction performed.
findings.recommendation: Give auxiliary store receipts a separate validated namespace or explicit record discriminator and add a native-profile supervisor restart regression preserving receipt and execution identities.

qualification_limits: Read-only source and retained-evidence review; root owns fresh gate and acceptance.

Retained final gate demonstrates actual shared/separate shell/apply_patch, namespace isolation, reconnect, restart restoration and lost-ACK recovery, but its confirmation crash hook covers thread/start only.
Model-free native protocol evidence does not establish live inference. Linked05/06 delivery, scoped TUI and live trial remain downstream.
